solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seedy growth of Brit rock on Oz radio?

indicators.note: heard over the airwaves in Australia, so the words are spoken in an Aussie accent

parts.note: a Pom is Australian slang for a Briton, and granite is a hard rock; together, said with an Australian twang, they come out as the fruit

explanation.surface: An Australian broadcaster asks what makes British rock music so seedy.
explanation.walkthrough: POM is Australian slang for a Briton; an Australian accent turns 'granite' into something like 'granate'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is famous for its many seeds, and it is something that grows on a tree.

clue.text: Ordinary patron's butt of gags halfway through for comedian

indicators.note: the letter is placed at the midpoint of the patron word, splitting it in two equal halves

parts.note: a punter is an ordinary customer or patron

indicators.note: the butt is the end, so the final letter of gags is taken

explanation.surface: A regular customer becomes the target of a stand-up's jokes midway through the set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halfway through' places the last letter of 'gags' exactly in the middle of the patron; 'butt' is the end, not the target of jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of wordplay jokes is a kind of comic entertainer.

clue.text: Consider — having left off central heating — bed cover

indicators.note: having left off means the letter for left is taken away from the word for consider

parts.note: to mull over is to consider

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about turning the heating off and piling a cover on the bed instead.
explanation.walkthrough: MULL loses one L to give MUL, then CH is added. The bed is a garden bed, not one in a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulch is a layer of compost or bark spread over a garden flowerbed to protect the soil.

clue.text: Crikey, embarrassing losing watch — it's a hunter!

parts.note: gosh and crikey are both mild exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: losing tells us a word for watch is dropped from the word for embarrassing

parts.note: an awkward situation is an embarrassing one
to ward is to guard or keep watch; a ward is also a watch or guard

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at an embarrassing moment of losing their wristwatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' drops a word for keeping watch, as in a ward or guard, from inside the embarrassing word; 'watch' is not a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: This large hawk is a bird of prey used in falconry to hunt.

clue.text: I'll get to the heart of confession of corruption that's all-enveloping

indicators.note: the letter will be placed in the very middle of the confession phrase

parts.note: a crooked person admitting guilt might say 'I am bent', giving AM BENT
I'll means I will, so the letter I is the piece that does the moving

explanation.surface: A detective vows to uncover the truth behind a corrupt official's admission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to the heart of' puts the I in the exact middle of the confession. BENT is British slang for corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes surroundings, conditions or sound that envelop one on every side.

clue.text: Cook prepares it right away, perhaps

definitions.text: Cook prepares it right away, perhaps

indicators.note: to cook the letters is to rework them into a new arrangement
away tells us one letter of the fodder is removed before the rest is rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef makes something at once, without waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R from PREPARESIT and rearrange the remaining nine letters. As a whole the clue describes a starter: a cook makes it to come first, straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter course is prepared by the cook and served first, before the main dish.

clue.text: Impressive flower for man of taste

parts.note: something epic is grand and impressive
a flower is something that flows, i.e. a river; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A gardener admires a grand bloom that would please a person of refined taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, here the Ure in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a connoisseur who takes refined pleasure in food and drink.

clue.text: 'Name' with advantage going round on stump

indicators.note: the advantage word goes round to the far side of on, so it is placed after it

parts.note: a plus is an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: A batsman gains an edge by walking round to the stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stump' is the verb meaning to baffle, not the cricket wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex or bewilder them, as a hard question does.

clue.text: Canoodle repeatedly, being close

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, to canoodle
repeatedly adds 'and' followed by the same verb again

explanation.surface: Two lovers kiss again and again, staying close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' asks for the kissing word again, joined by AND.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a race or contest so tight that neither rival is ahead.

clue.text: Roll with ends of tahini and odd bits of some divine dip?

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

indicators.note: the first and last letters of tahini are taken
the first and third letters of some are taken, the odd-numbered ones

explanation.surface: A bread roll is served with tahini and a few other bits of a delicious dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine dip' is a playful way to describe a religious immersion; a hummus-style dip is what the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening involves sprinkling or immersing a person in holy water, a sacred dipping.

clue.text: Fashion requirement for tennis is to be loud

parts.note: to fashion something is to make it
a tennis player needs a racket

explanation.surface: A style guide insists that the tennis look must be showy and loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' is a verb here, not the clothing world.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to create a lot of noise and disturbance.

clue.text: This 22's tricky to get

definitions.meaning: on its own the word means a hidden snag or tricky trap
to get something thrown or understand a remark is to grasp or receive it

explanation.surface: A puzzle of this kind is hard to solve.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' points at the Joseph Heller title Catch-22.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a hidden snag, and as a verb means to seize or grasp.

clue.text: Terrified of Nato allies, say, getting caught in leader of America's fight

indicators.note: the allies are trapped inside the other pieces
the leader is the first letter of America's

parts.note: a ruck is a scuffle or brawl
the Western powers make up Nato, so they are the West

explanation.surface: People are frightened of Western allies being drawn into America's war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting caught in' puts the allies inside the other two pieces, just after America's first letter; 'caught' is not the cricket C.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with awe, a mixture of wonder and fear, close to terrified.

clue.text: What's on your 'ead? A bit of it may be what's blocking pipe!

parts.note: hair is on your head; dropping the H, as in 'ead, gives AIR
a lock is a small bunch of hair

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks what grows on your head and suggests some may clog a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ead tells you to drop the H from HAIR too. Hair in a plughole is the surface joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubble of trapped gas stops liquid flowing through a pipe or hose.

clue.text: Privatise public water supply

parts.note: if something is out, it is public or known
a source is where a stream or water supply begins

explanation.surface: A government sells off the public water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public water supply' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracting work to private outside firms is a way of privatising a service.

clue.text: Queen interrupting property being returned — a classical piece of marble?

indicators.note: the Queen breaks into the reversed property word
returned means the property word is read backwards

parts.note: an asset is a piece of property
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen steps in as a property returns a classical marble sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being returned' reverses the property word to TESSA, and 'interrupting' puts the Queen inside it near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square tiles of stone or glass in a Roman mosaic.

clue.text: One making initial report increasingly absurd about Republican

indicators.note: the absurd word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: dafter means sillier, more absurd

explanation.surface: A journalist's first report about a Republican grows ever more ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside DAFTER, after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes a first version of a document produces an early draft.

clue.text: What one does with bolt-on as program shuts down

parts.note: an app is a computer program
ends means finishes or shuts down

explanation.surface: A user installs an add-on and the program shuts down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt-on' is an extra added at the end, as attached text or software.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach an extra item, as one fixes on an add-on.

clue.text: Transform marketing of beer brewed around centre of Wigan after advert

indicators.note: the brewed letters go round the other pieces
brewing turns the letters of beer into a new mix
the middle letter of Wigan comes after the advert

parts.note: AD is a short form of advertisement

indicators.note: the centre of Wigan is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A brewery relaunches its beer brand in Wigan after an advertising campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' scrambles the beer to REBE, which goes 'around' the advert followed by G. Wigan is a town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebadging means selling a product under a new brand name or logo, changing how it is marketed.

clue.text: It's helpful to climbers thus to enter mountain from the east

indicators.note: the Latin-derived word goes inside the mountain
in an across entry, read from the east means right to left, backwards

parts.note: an Alp is a high mountain
ergo is Latin for therefore or thus

explanation.surface: Mountaineers find it useful to enter a peak from its eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the east' reverses the mountain to PLA, and 'to enter' puts the Latin word inside. 'Climbers' are plants, not mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden arbour of posts and trellis supports climbing plants such as roses.

clue.text: Ineffectual treatment of rank bad smell

parts.note: a place is a position or rank
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A useless cure for a foul stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective for the smell but is a noun for position.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill with no active drug is given in place of real medicine.

clue.text: Rhetoric of a Labourite __ __ __?

parts.note: the three gaps want a pair of small words and a party member opposed to Labour, completing a choice between Britain's two main parties; the filled phrase is also a word for rhetoric

explanation.surface: A question about the speechmaking style of a Labour politician, with a blank to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour and the Conservatives (Tories) are Britain's two big parties; the blanks take three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of public speaking and eloquent persuasion is a synonym of rhetoric.

clue.text: Joy drinking essence of zebra plant

indicators.note: joy swallows the letter taken from zebra

parts.note: euphoria is intense joy

indicators.note: the essence is the central letter

explanation.surface: Joy comes from a zebra drinking from a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinking' means the joy word swallows the zebra's central letter; 'plant' is the definition, the surface's watering hole aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The spurges are a large genus of plants with milky sap, including the poinsettia.

clue.text: Animate short cartoon on TV?

indicators.note: the first word is cut short to its initial

parts.note: South Park is an American animated television series

explanation.surface: A brief animated cartoon brings the TV screen to life.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTH is abbreviated to S, as on a compass, leaving S PARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to enliven or excite, as a spark sets something off.

clue.text: Well-oiled on ship — bottoms up!

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: keels are the bottoms of ships

explanation.surface: A drunken sailor aboard ship raises a toast: bottoms up!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-oiled' means drunk on the surface, but the answer takes its 'smooth and glossy' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy, smooth hair or fur looks as though it has been oiled.

clue.text: Agreeable Shiraz, say, for family

parts.note: kind means pleasant and agreeable
Shiraz is an example of red wine

explanation.surface: A pleasant bottle of Shiraz shared with relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Shiraz as one example of a red.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred are one's relatives, people related by blood.

clue.text: Equalise, still getting disqualified

parts.note: even can mean still, as in 'even more' and 'still more'
a disqualified player is out

explanation.surface: A team equalises yet still gets thrown out of the competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' as in 'even better' becomes EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To level things off or remove differences makes them equal.

clue.text: Bob maybe having vital 'Access all areas' pass?

parts.note: the bobsleigh and the skeleton are both winter sliding sports, so bob is an example of the sort of sled race
a key factor is a vital one

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob has a backstage pass to get everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; it is the bobsleigh, a sliding sport like the skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: A master key that opens many different locks lets the holder in everywhere.
